classes.name: Alpha-1 blockers
classes.description: Alpha-1 blockers for BPH: tamsulosin (Flomax), alfuzosin ER (Uroxatral), silodosin (Rapaflo), doxazosin (Cardura; Cardura XL is brand-only), terazosin. Combination dutasteride/tamsulosin (Jalyn) belongs to the 5-ARI class.
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill that relaxes the prostate so urine flows more easily.

classes.name: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors
classes.description: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors for BPH: finasteride 5 mg (Proscar), dutasteride (Avodart), dutasteride/tamsulosin (Jalyn), finasteride/tadalafil (Entadfi; up to 26 weeks, not with alpha blockers). The pick is a single agent; the combinations are alternatives. Finasteride 1 mg (Propecia, hair loss) is not this class.
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill that slowly shrinks an enlarged prostate over months.

classes.name: Tadalafil for BPH
classes.description: Tadalafil 2.5 mg and 5 mg once daily (Cialis, generic) for BPH symptoms. Plans often cover it for BPH only with a diagnosis-based PA and exclude it for erectile dysfunction: record the BPH rule. Sildenafil and vardenafil are not labeled for BPH.
classes.plainDescription: A low daily dose of tadalafil that eases urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate.

preferredAgent.sig: 0.4 mg by mouth once daily, 30 minutes after the same meal each day; may increase to 0.8 mg once daily after 2 to 4 weeks (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One capsule a day, 30 minutes after the same meal.

records.verificationNote: PDL p.35 'BPH AGENTS': tamsulosin, alfuzosin, CARDURA, CARDURA XL, doxazosin and terazosin preferred. FLOMAX, RAPAFLO, silodosin and TEZRULY non-preferred. Generic tamsulosin preferred over FLOMAX, so no BOGL flag. PDL prints no form; capsule assumed. Strength 0.4 mg per brief.

preferredAgent.sig: 5 mg by mouth once daily for BPH (label). Benefit builds over 6 to 12 months.

records.verificationNote: PDL p.35 '5-ALPHA-REDUCTASE (5AR) INHIBITORS': finasteride preferred; dutasteride and PROSCAR non-preferred. records.verificationNote: PDL p.35 'PHOSPHODIESTERASE 5 INHIBITORS' (BPH section) lists no preferred agent; tadalafil is the only item, in the non-preferred column (p.36). PDL p.35 states: 'For drugs in a therapeutic class or subclass with no preferred option, the provider must obtain a PDL prior authorization.' Sildenafil and vardenafil are not in the BPH section (sildenafil appears only in the PAH section, p.73). CIALIS is not in the PDL. Diagnosis-based criteria (BPH vs erectile dysfunction) are not stated in the PDL and not inferred.

The list does not state a BPH-only indication for this line; the 10/20 mg Cialis ED line is p+ (group-specific) and is not the BPH pick.
